limits: One reader. This adjudication is a single lane on claude-opus-5-5, a recorded fallback for the model OW-13 assigned to this role. The proposer, every Daniel lane whose packet is cited, and the ruling role ran on the same model. My agreement with the proposer on all eight ratings is one voice, not two (OW-19).

Evidence was read through truncated script extracts of named rulings, gate fields, uncertainty entries and single routed lines, not through whole packets. A sentence later in a ruling than my extract could qualify what I quote.

Counts I did not produce by script are quoted as the source's own and marked EXTRACTED as to what the file says; their truth is REPORTED. This holds for the 49 of 75 rows (E3), the 16 zone hits (E2), the 1, 2 and 28 changed places (boss audit B3) and the 15 of 17 conditions.

Counts I did produce: ten of eleven primary packets with a keyword hit (a keyword scan, not a reading of meaning); thirteen blocked entries across five landed6 change files; zero strategy lines with certain words. Each is MEASURED by work/q.py of this execution and is no stronger than its keyword.
I did not read rows_v1_final.jsonl or its manifest beyond hashing them, so no claim about the closed rows themselves is mine. I did not re-measure the proposer's language census.
The book strategy was searched by line for keywords and not read whole. Where I say the strategy does not state a rule, I mean that no line holds the words I searched for.

For proposals with more than three cited artefacts I opened at least two and not all. In Dan-P04, two of seven E9 rulings; in Dan-P03, two of ten packet hits in words; in Dan-P05 and Dan-P08, one or two of the cited packets per group.

Every adopted text prescribes a control Daniel did not run. Section 13 of v6 warns that an untested rule is worse than an open question; I have marked each such control untried inside its text and asked the first book that runs it to record the result. Whether that is enough to enter them in v7 as rules and not as open questions is a judgement the owner or the architect role may wish to revisit.

Dan-P05: I did not adopt the content of the rule on what opens a repair round; I named two floors for it. Naming floors is itself a judgement, taken from E6 CLASS-TIER-WORD and section 18, and may be overruled.

Fix-up rounds 7 to 10 were seen only through rulings E8 to E12, re-review packets and the boss audit. The proposer's notes record that the manifest paths of those rounds' change logs are malformed; I did not try to open them.
Two tool results exceeded the display limit and were read back from the tool-results files the harness wrote; those are my own script output, not campaign files.
